items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: back in '34 when I had Garnet Clark playing piano up there

ctx.x: The reason probably was pressure, wasn't it, or was it?

Well, you see, I had never had any pressure that way, because I had never tried to do it, and I never got any pressure back in '34 when I had Garnet Clark playing piano up there and Benny Carter sitting back in the trumpet section on certain nights. I never heard a word from the management about it. You see, I never ran into this, and somehow or other I tend to find some of these stories must be greatly exaggerated. Maybe -- maybe these curious people that I'm talking about were met with some kind of antagonism,…

Do you suppose that maybe your attitude had something to do with it, that you took it or accepted it as curiosity, and therefore it didn't go in the wrong direction, whereas someone else took it as hostility?
